criteria.description: After reading it the student knows what to do next, and it deals with what they actually asked or need, including the real problem behind the question.

criteria.description: It leaves the thinking to the student at the instructor's support level: no copyable solution, and the amount of help fits the level.

Questions that are not the student's own task (definitions, course logistics, what a lecture says) may be answered directly at any level. achieved: respects the no-solution rule and the level's amount of help. partly_achieved: slightly too much or too little help for the level, or a hint that comes close to the fix. not_achieved: hands over the solution or copyable work, gives long explanations at low support, or refuses an ordinary factual question.

reference: FACT: The video (unit 7001) at 312.5 s, about 5:12, says the recursion tree has log n levels and each level performs linear merge work. The slide shown (page 8) gives T(n)=2T(n/2)+Theta(n), hence Theta(n log n).

FACT: Linear work at every level means the merge work done across all subproblems at one level adds up to about n: subproblems get smaller but more numerous. With log n levels the total is n times log n, matching Theta(n log n) on the slide. The Theta(n) term in the recurrence is that per-level cost.
FACT: The lecture's Master Theorem section (a=2, b=2, f(n)=Theta(n), case 2) gives the same Theta(n log n), which is a place to point the student for a cross-check.
NEED: The student asks what the lecturer means right now, at this point of the video. They need the phrase explained in terms of the tree and tied to the n log n result on the visible slide.

HOLD BACK: Support is moderate: explain the concept and point to the slide and the video moment, with a small hint or question for the student to complete. Do not turn it into a full formal proof of the bound.
